# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

</system-reminder>

I also want to trace which script seeded the terraria GameMod rows, likely the Steam Workshop catalog importer using appid 1281930.

I should also check the production DB to see if any ServerMod rows reference these terraria GameMods — if live customers have installed or failed entries tied to them, deleting the GameMod rows could break foreign key references. I'll run read-only psql queries using credentials from .env to check this carefully before making changes.

There are two real customer terraria servers I must not touch: terraria-i2ydef and throarbin-terraria. Since existing containers won't retroactively get the new bind mount from setupScript, adding terraria to INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES would expose an Install button on these two customers' containers that lack the mount, risking a broken install into /opt/terraria.

The safe fix is having modDirShell actually verify the live container's mounts via docker inspect for the /tshock/ServerPlugins destination, returning NODIR with a clear error if it's missing rather than faking success — this way the check is self-verifying against the real container state instead of assuming the mount exists.

I also need to remember TShock doesn't hot-load plugins like Rust/Oxide does — it needs a restart, so the panel must surface a "restart required" message, which means checking how the mods UI currently communicates that. Before touching anything, I want to inspect the actual ryshe/terraria image, likely by provisioning a real test VM since Proxmox itself shouldn't run docker directly, and recalling how its Dockerfile lays out the tshock installation.

The bootstrap.sh script actually copies everything from `/plugins` into `./ServerPlugins` at container startup, which mirrors the Valheim drop-in mechanism I was thinking of. That confirms the safer fix is bind-mounting the host directory to `/plugins` rather than `/tshock/ServerPlugins`, since the image's default plugins stay intact and only custom ones get merged in at boot.

But this raises a removal problem: since the copy step never deletes files, an uninstalled plugin removed from `/plugins` would still persist inside `ServerPlugins` across restarts because that directory lives in the container's writable layer. So uninstalling would need an explicit follow-up step, like execing into the container to remove the specific file from `ServerPlugins` directly.

I also need to check this against the actual image and its config volume setup, and confirm how TShock 5.x structures ServerPlugins — since if TShockAPI.dll itself lives there and gets wiped by an empty bind-mount, the server would just boot vanilla with no TShock loaded at all.

That's the real risk, and using /plugins instead avoids it. Since the task wants me to verify whether that risk is real and explain how I'm handling it, I should check the image on Docker Hub/GitHub, provision a real test server, and look at how the admin grants a free server for testing via lib/actions.ts and scripts/e2e-test.ts.

80	/**
81	 * The generalization this file's own docstring called for: substitute a
82	 * customer's checkout-time `Server.gameConfig` values into an OsTemplate's
83	 * setupScript, for whichever fields already appear in it as a docker
84	 * `-e KEY=...` env-var placeholder.
85	 *
86	 * Found live 2026-08-31 auditing DST (`dst` family): the whole per-family
87	 * customization schema in lib/game-config.ts (`ConfigField`, one per
88	 * `docker run -e KEY=...` in prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts and its Wave 1-3
89	 * predecessors) is captured at checkout into `Server.gameConfig`
90	 * (lib/game-order.ts) and shown in the post-deploy Settings tab, but — same
91	 * root cause as `applyGameVariant` above, just never generalized —
92	 * `provision()` in worker/index.ts never read it. Every family's setup
93	 * script always ran with its hardcoded static default (usually `''`),
94	 * regardless of what the customer entered at checkout. For most fields that
95	 * meant a cosmetically-wrong default (wrong MOTD, wrong hostname string);
96	 * for DST's `TOKEN` (an online DST cluster refuses to start with none — see
97	 * lib/game-config.ts's DST schema comment) it meant the container never
98	 * bound its port at all and PROVISION's own `checkGamePortOpen` health check
99	 * would time out and hard-fail the customer's paid order.
100	 *
101	 * Deliberately conservative: ONLY touches a key if the setupScript already
102	 * declares it as `-e KEY=...` — fields with no such placeholder (e.g. DST's
103	 * `PASSWORD`, which the yeetzone image never wired to an env var at all) are
104	 * left untouched rather than guessing a docker flag that isn't there.
105	 * Values are re-quoted as a single-quoted shell literal with proper `'`
106	 * escaping (`'\''`) so a customer-supplied string can never break out of the
107	 * quote and inject shell — the same safety property `validateConfig`'s own
108	 * control-character guard exists for, just extended to this second consumer
109	 * (a `docker run` command line) since the injection surface differs from a
110	 * line-oriented remote config file.
111	 */
112	/**
113	 * Substitute a freshly generated per-server secret into an OsTemplate's
114	 * setupScript, for a family whose image needs a real secret value that the
115	 * static catalog row can only ever leave blank — baking one directly into
116	 * the shared seed string (prisma/catalog.ts) would hand every future
117	 * customer the exact SAME value, since that row is one string shared by
118	 * every server of that family.
119	 *
120	 * Found live 2026-09-05 fixing a customer's "player list never loads"
121	 * ticket: the platform's own player-list/RCON feature (lib/game-control.ts)
122	 * requires Palworld's ADMIN_PASSWORD to be set (it doubles as the RCON auth
123	 * secret) and RCON's port published, but the catalog's setupScript set
124	 * neither — so no Palworld server, ever provisioned, could support the
125	 * player-list feature customers are paying for. RCON_ENABLED/RCON_PORT are
126	 * not secrets, so those went directly into prisma/catalog.ts's setupScript
127	 * string; only this one per-server value needs runtime substitution.
128	 *
129	 * Same conservative shape as applyGameConfigEnv: only touches a key that's
130	 * already present as `-e KEY=...` in the script, and the caller decides what
131	 * counts as a "secret" for a given family — this function has no per-family
132	 * knowledge of its own.
133	 */
134	export function applyGameControlSecrets(
135	  setupScript: string,
136	  secrets: Record<string, string>,
137	): string {
138	  let out = setupScript;
139	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(secrets)) {
140	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${key}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
141	    if (!re.test(out)) continue;
142	    const escaped = value.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
143	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${key}='${escaped}'`);
144	  }
145	  return out;
146	}
147	
148	export function applyGameConfigEnv(
149	  setupScript: string,
150	  family: string | null,
151	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
152	): string {
153	  if (!family || !gameConfig) return setupScript;
154	  const schema = schemaFor(family);
155	  if (!schema) return setupScript;
156	  let out = setupScript;
157	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
158	    const raw = gameConfig[field.key];
159	    if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;
160	    // envKey lets a readable schema key (e.g. "world") differ from the
161	    // literal docker env var name the image expects (e.g. "WORLD_NAME") —
162	    // see ConfigField.envKey's doc comment in lib/game-config.ts.
163	    const envName = field.envKey ?? field.key;
164	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${envName}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
165	    if (!re.test(out)) continue; // this field isn't docker-env-driven in this script — leave it alone
166	    const escaped = String(raw).replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
167	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${envName}='${escaped}'`);
168	  }
169	  return out;
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * If a GAME OsTemplate's setupScript installs the game via a detached
174	 * `docker run -d --name <container> ...` (true for every game image today —
175	 * see the OsTemplate rows for minecraft/terraria/ark/etc., all `docker run -d`),
176	 * rewrite the invocation to `docker create` and append a generated systemd unit
177	 * that starts/stops the container. Also caps the container's log driver
178	 * (`--log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3`) — see the comment at the
179	 * `createCmd` line below for why.
180	 *
181	 * WHY THIS EXISTS: the whole game control panel — GAME_POWER start/stop/restart,
182	 * GAME_BACKUP, log tailing (lib/game-control.ts + worker/game-control.ts) —
183	 * resolves the running game exclusively via `systemctl cat <serviceHint>` /
184	 * `journalctl -u <unit>`. A bare `docker run -d` creates no systemd unit at all,
185	 * so every one of those lookups comes back empty and every control action fails
186	 * silently, on every game family, on every order. Found 2026-08-26 diagnosing a
187	 * customer's Terraria server (cmt9ss7ln000xhlrx0gch9fcx) that could never be
188	 * started/stopped from the dashboard even though PROVISION had completed
189	 * successfully — the container was in fact running, just entirely invisible to
190	 * systemd.
191	 *
192	 * The generated unit is named after the family's FIRST serviceHint, not the
193	 * docker container's own `--name` — the two don't always match (minecraft's
194	 * image runs as container "mc" but its control-spec hints are "minecraft" /
195	 * "minecraft-server") — so `systemctl cat <hint>` resolves regardless of what an
196	 * individual image's setup script happened to call its container.
197	 *
198	 * Intentionally conservative: any setupScript that doesn't match the exact
199	 * `docker run -d --name X ...` shape (or any non-game family, e.g. the
200	 * LAMP/WordPress/Caddy panel images that already install a real native systemd
201	 * service) is returned completely unchanged.
202	 *
203	 * Moved here from worker/index.ts 2026-09-24 (alongside `buildGameSetupScript`
204	 * below) so worker/game-control.ts — which worker/index.ts itself imports, so
205	 * it cannot import anything back from worker/index.ts without a circular
206	 * dependency — can also build a real reinstall script for the Danger Zone's
207	 * wipe/reinstall action. Purely a relocation: behavior is unchanged.
208	 */
209	export function wrapDockerGameService(setupScript: string, family: string | null): string {
210	  if (!isGameFamily(family)) return setupScript;
211	  const unitName = controlSpec(family)?.serviceHints[0];
212	  if (!unitName) return setupScript;
213	
214	  const re = /docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b(.*?)\s+--name[= ]("?)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\2(.*)$/.exec(setupScript.trim());
215	  if (!re) return setupScript;
216	  const [full, before, , containerName, after] = re;
217	  const matchIndex = setupScript.indexOf(full);
218	  if (matchIndex < 0) return setupScript;
219	
220	  // Strip docker's own restart policy — systemd now owns restart semantics for
221	  // this container, and leaving both in place makes the two supervisors fight
222	  // over a crash-looping process.
223	  const cleanedAfter = after.replace(/\s*--restart(?:=|\s+)\S+/, "");
224	  // Cap the container's json-file log driver. No game image's setupScript ever
225	  // set this, so a crash-looping container (systemd restarting it every 5s
226	  // forever — see RestartSec above) grows an unbounded log file. Root-caused
227	  // live 2026-09-17 on projectzomboid-kc0kcr: its docker json log alone had
228	  // grown to ~28 GB (on top of ~28.5 GB of rsyslog spamming its own
229	  // "no space left on device" write failures once the disk filled), filling
230	  // the 77 GB root disk to 100% and taking the game server down. This is the
231	  // single construction point every game family's `docker run` is rewritten
232	  // through, so applying the cap here covers all of them at once rather than
233	  // editing each family's setupScript individually. 10m x 3 files = a 30 MB
234	  // ceiling per container regardless of how long or how hard it crash-loops.
235	  const createCmd = `docker create --name ${containerName} --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3${before}${cleanedAfter}`
236	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
237	    .trim();
238	
239	  const prefix = setupScript.slice(0, matchIndex);
240	  const unit = [
241	    `cat > /etc/systemd/system/${unitName}.service <<'NXUNIT'`,
242	    "[Unit]",
243	    `Description=Nxeon game service (docker: ${containerName})`,
244	    "After=docker.service",
245	    "Requires=docker.service",
246	    "",
247	    "[Service]",
248	    `ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker start -a ${containerName}`,
249	    `ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker stop -t 30 ${containerName}`,
250	    "Restart=always",
251	    "RestartSec=5",
252	    "TimeoutStartSec=0",
253	    "",
254	    "[Install]",
255	    "WantedBy=multi-user.target",
256	    "NXUNIT",
257	    "systemctl daemon-reload",
258	    `systemctl enable --now ${unitName}`,

260	
261	  return `${prefix}${createCmd}\n${unit}`;

I'm realizing that gameReinstall pulls the setup script from the DB template, so once the catalog change is deployed and rerun, existing customers could only get the mod via "Wipe & reinstall," which wipes their world — for them the install should just fail honestly rather than silently work around that.

Also, gameReinstall wipes host mounts entirely, including the plugins directory, so ServerMod rows could show INSTALLED even though the files are gone — this is a pre-existing issue across families like Minecraft and Terraria, not something in my scope, but worth flagging.

Since I don't want to touch the shared prod OsTemplate row before review, for the "after" verification on real hardware I'm considering manually running the exact new setup script — generated via a small script that imports buildGameSetupScript with my new setupScript string — after stopping the stock container, so it exercises the same docker create and systemd unit logic the worker would actually run.

Provisioning a second VM with a new temporary OsTemplate row feels riskier since some code might query the first template by family and inadvertently pick it up, so running the generated script directly on a fresh VM (mirroring what cloud-init would execute) seems like the safer, sufficiently faithful test.

Actually, an even better approach: since /opt/terraria already exists on my test server, wiping it would effectively simulate what gameReinstall does, so I could call gameModSync and gameReinstall directly from my worktree against the prod DB for just my test server — but I need to avoid creating real Job rows, since the old prod worker would pick those up and fail with outdated code. Instead I should invoke gameModSync directly with a synthetic job object that only references job.serverId, bypassing the Job table entirely.

Now I need a ServerMod row with INSTALLING status and a GameMod row pointing to a real TShock plugin from github, which raises the question of whether to reseed the whole prod catalog now or just write the seed script for the owner to run later — since the task says not to merge or promote, and reseeding would expose new github-based rows in the prod UI while prod code still treats terraria as non-installable.

I'm leaning toward delivering the reseed as an idempotent, dry-run-by-default script guarded by an environment variable, applying it for real on staging but only dry-running it against prod, leaving the actual prod run to the owner at promote time. But for testing the real install path on hardware, I still need actual GameMod and ServerMod rows the worker can read, which means pointing my worktree's gameModSync at the prod database directly since that's where the test server lives.

My plan is to create a temporary GameMod row marked inactive so it stays out of the catalog UI, plus a matching ServerMod row for my test server, run the sync to exercise the full install path including DB status updates and notifications, then clean both rows up afterward. I'm also checking whether inactive GameMod rows are actually filtered out by catalog queries, and figuring out which test user should own the server so notifications land somewhere sensible.

I should use a dedicated test account rather than the admin account, checking if something like "e2e-test@nxeon.local" already exists. For node placement, I want to explicitly pick a node like node-2 rather than letting the scheduler choose, and I need to check current node load/capacity while making sure never to reuse an existing VMID.

Vmid allocation and port-forwarding for the game port with health checks are already handled by the real provisioning worker, so I don't need to reimplement that logic. Let me look at the production database next to see the available nodes, test users, and Terraria game plans.

#!/bin/bash

echo "\nBootstrap:\nworld_file_name=$WORLD_FILENAME\nconfigpath=$CONFIGPATH\nlogpath=$LOGPATH\n"

# Copy plugins if the folder is empty (like on first run)
if [ -z "$(ls -A /tshock/ServerPlugins)" ]; then

  cp /plugins/* /tshock/ServerPlugins
fi

if [ $(jq -r '.Settings.StorageType' $CONFIGPATH/config.json) = "mysql" ]; then

  DATABASE_PORT=$(jq -r '.Settings.MySqlHost' $CONFIGPATH/config.json | cut -f2 -d':')
  DATABASE_USER_NAME=$(jq -r '.Settings.MySqlUsername' $CONFIGPATH/config.json)
  DATABASE_USER_PASSWORD=$(jq -r '.Settings.MySqlPassword' $CONFIGPATH/config.json)

    sleep 0.1
  done
fi

WORLD_PATH="/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds/$WORLD_FILENAME"

autocreate_flag=false
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "-autocreate" ]; then
    autocreate_flag=true
    break
  fi
done

if [ -z "$WORLD_FILENAME" ]; then
  echo "No world file specified in environment WORLD_FILENAME."
  if [ -z "$@" ]; then
    echo "Running server setup..."
  else
    echo "Running server with command flags: $@"
  fi
  ./TShock.Server -configpath "$CONFIGPATH" -logpath "$LOGPATH" "$@"
else

    echo "Alternatively, use the -autocreate flag to create a new world."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

---
name: nxeon-worktree-nodemodules-hazard
description: "NEVER git add -A in a worktree that has a node_modules symlink — it can destroy prod's real node_modules"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc
  modified: 2026-08-21T17:19:08.560Z
---

On 2026-08-21 I nearly took prod down. In a worktree I created `node_modules` as a symlink to `/opt/nxeon/node_modules` (the standard setup), then ran `git add -A` which COMMITTED the symlink (`.gitignore` has `node_modules/` with a trailing slash, which does NOT match a symlink named `node_modules`). Fast-forwarding that commit into the prod tree `/opt/nxeon` replaced its **real** `node_modules` directory with a **self-referential symlink** (`/opt/nxeon/node_modules -> /opt/nxeon/node_modules`), deleting 1.1G of packages. `next` and the Prisma client became unresolvable; only the in-memory running services survived.

**Why:** never stage the whole tree in a symlinked worktree.
**How to apply:**
- In worktrees, `git add` ONLY the specific files you changed — never `git add -A` / `git add .`.
- Recovery if it happens: `git rm --cached node_modules && rm -f node_modules` in the prod tree, then `npm ci` (lockfile present) + `npx prisma generate`, then commit the untracking. Do this BEFORE any restart/promote — running services hold modules in memory but a build/restart will fail hard.
- Consider hardening `.gitignore` with a bare `node_modules` line (no slash) so the symlink is ignored too.

Relates to [[nxeon-build-isolation]] and the deploy flow in [[nxeon-resume-point]].

import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const globalForPrisma = globalThis as unknown as { prisma?: PrismaClient };

export const db = globalForPrisma.prisma ?? new PrismaClient();

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") globalForPrisma.prisma = db;
/**
 * Refuse to write to a database nobody deliberately pointed us at.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE INCIDENT THIS EXISTS FOR (2026-07-26)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * An agent ran `prisma/seed.ts` from a scratch working tree. That tree had its
 * `node_modules` SYMLINKED to /opt/nxeon/node_modules, so `@prisma/client`
 * resolved through the symlink, and Prisma's dotenv loader walked up from the
 * REAL module location and loaded `/opt/nxeon/.env` — the PRODUCTION env. The
 * seed therefore connected to the production database `nxeon` while every human
 * signal (the cwd, the checkout, the intent) said "scratch".
 *
 * It happened to be a pure `upsert` seed, so it did no damage. That is luck, not
 * a control. The same accident with `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`, or with
 * a seed that had grown a `deleteMany`, destroys a live hosting platform's
 * customer records.
 *
 * The root cause is NOT "the seed was careless". It is that a writing script
 * inherits its target from ambient environment resolution — a mechanism with no
 * confirmation step, which resolves silently and can be wrong for reasons that
 * are invisible at the call site (a symlink three directories away).
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE CONTROL
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * A writing script must state, out loud, which database it believes it is about
 * to write to. The operator states it independently, via `NXEON_DB_TARGET`. The
 * script runs only if the two agree.
 *
 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed.ts
 *
 * This is deliberately NOT a "--force"/"--yes" flag. A blanket confirmation
 * answers "do you want to proceed?", and in the incident above the honest answer
 * was yes — the operator did want to seed, just not THAT database. Naming the
 * target answers the question that was actually wrong. An operator who types
 * `NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_scratch` while the environment silently resolves to
 * `nxeon` gets a refusal and a diff, which is exactly the moment the symlink
 * becomes visible.
 *
 * Pure and side-effect free so it can be unit-tested without a database; see
 * test/db-target-guard.test.ts.
 */

/** Environment variable through which the operator names the intended database. */
export const TARGET_ENV_VAR = "NXEON_DB_TARGET";

export type DbTargetDecision =
  | { allowed: true; database: string }
  | { allowed: false; database: string | null; message: string };

content.thinking:
A broken plugin's load failure can throw an exception that halts the entire server init, and with systemd set to always restart, that becomes a crash loop taking down the customer's server. So I should only seed plugins verified against the current image, and have the worker check after restart that the port is actually bound, rolling back by removing the installed file if it isn't.

Version drift matters too: customers on older images (TShock 5.x, .NET 6) vs newer ones (TShock 6.1, .NET 9) means a plugin built for a newer runtime simply won't load on an older container, making rollback verification essential. I'm planning to reuse the worker's existing port-check helpers and, since game-mods has its own SSH transport, do the restart and log-polling over SSH — checking for a "Server started" success marker or known failure strings like "Failed to load assembly" to decide whether to roll back.

But I realize pinpointing whether a *specific* plugin loaded is trickier: TShock's API-version mismatch warning logs the type name, not the filename, so matching it back to the installed file isn't straightforward without extra tooling on the VM.

A more practical fallback: if the load-failure error mentions the deterministic filename directly, roll back that specific plugin; if the server just fails to boot after a batch install, roll back everything in that batch and mark all as failed. For the silent "ignored due to API mismatch" case, I could compare the list of "Plugin X vY initiated" lines before and after the change to infer which plugin didn't register.

Doing this incrementally per mod would be the most reliable, but restarting the server for every single mod is expensive time-wise, so I need to weigh that tradeoff against batch installs where attribution is fuzzier.

I'm now thinking about matching names differently: the assembly load failure message gives the actual filename, but the API-version warning only gives the type's full name, and the successful init line only gives the plugin's display name—so these three don't share a common key I can join on directly, and parsing the DLL metadata myself would be overkill.

Instead, I'm considering a diff-based approach: capture the container's startup timestamp, grab the set of "initiated" plugin lines from logs since that point as the baseline, then after the restart pull logs from the new startup time and treat any newly appearing initiated lines as the plugins that installed successfully.

For the typical single-mod job this is clean — one or more new initiated lines means it loaded, zero means it was silently ignored (likely an API-version mismatch) so I'd roll it back and report incompatibility. For batch jobs I'm weighing whether to process installs one restart at a time rather than trying to reconcile counts across a mixed batch, since that's simpler to reason about correctly.

Stepping back, though, I should check whether the actual task scope even requires this level of verification — it may just want the terraria case added to modDirShell following the same SFTP placement pattern, with TShock's lack of hot-loading being a separate concern.

### bootstrap.sh (from the running image)
#!/bin/bash

echo "\nBootstrap:\nworld_file_name=$WORLD_FILENAME\nconfigpath=$CONFIGPATH\nlogpath=$LOGPATH\n"

# Copy plugins if the folder is empty (like on first run)
if [ -z "$(ls -A /tshock/ServerPlugins)" ]; then
  echo "Copying plugins..."
  cp /plugins/* /tshock/ServerPlugins
fi

if [ $(jq -r '.Settings.StorageType' $CONFIGPATH/config.json) = "mysql" ]; then
  DATABASE_SERVER=$(jq -r '.Settings.MySqlHost' $CONFIGPATH/config.json | cut -f1 -d':')
  DATABASE_PORT=$(jq -r '.Settings.MySqlHost' $CONFIGPATH/config.json | cut -f2 -d':')
  DATABASE_USER_NAME=$(jq -r '.Settings.MySqlUsername' $CONFIGPATH/config.json)
  DATABASE_USER_PASSWORD=$(jq -r '.Settings.MySqlPassword' $CONFIGPATH/config.json)
  echo "Waiting for the database server."
  while ! mysql -h$DATABASE_SERVER -P$DATABASE_PORT -u$DATABASE_USER_NAME -p$DATABASE_USER_PASSWORD -e ";"; do
    sleep 0.1
  done
fi

WORLD_PATH="/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds/$WORLD_FILENAME"

autocreate_flag=false
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "-autocreate" ]; then
    autocreate_flag=true
    break
  fi
done

if [ -z "$WORLD_FILENAME" ]; then
  echo "No world file specified in environment WORLD_FILENAME."
  if [ -z "$@" ]; then
    echo "Running server setup..."
  else
    echo "Running server with command flags: $@"
  fi
  ./TShock.Server -configpath "$CONFIGPATH" -logpath "$LOGPATH" "$@"
else
  echo "Environment WORLD_FILENAME specified"
  if [ -f "$WORLD_PATH" ] || [ "$autocreate_flag" = true ]; then
    echo "Loading to world $WORLD_FILENAME..."
    ./TShock.Server -configpath "$CONFIGPATH" -logpath "$LOGPATH" -world "$WORLD_PATH" "$@"
  else
    echo "Unable to locate $WORLD_PATH and -autocreate flag is not set."
    echo "Please make sure your world file is volumed into docker: -v <path_to_world_file>:/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds"
    echo "Alternatively, use the -autocreate flag to create a new world."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

content.thinking:
I'm confirming that bootstrap.sh only repopulates /tshock/ServerPlugins with TShockAPI files when the host-mounted folder is empty on first run — so an empty bind-mounted directory would get the plugins copied back in, but a directory that already contains any file (like a customer's own plugin) at boot time behaves differently.

Now I want to actually verify this on the real container rather than just reasoning about it, since the task calls for validating the scoped change. I'll test the standard case — recreating the container with the empty host directory mounted to ServerPlugins, confirming bootstrap repopulates defaults and TShock starts, then dropping in a plugin and restarting to confirm it loads — and also test the risky edge case where the directory is emptied except for a leftover plugin file at boot, to see whether TShock's core files fail to get copied and the server comes up broken.

I'm also thinking through the realistic paths that could actually produce that hazardous "non-empty but missing TShockAPI" state: a customer manually deleting or renaming the DLL via the file manager, or an image upgrade where TShock.Server gets bumped but a stale TShockAPI.dll persists because the container isn't re-pulled today (though a customer could force it via SSH, or a future auto-update feature could introduce it). Existing servers without this mount would only hit it via a reinstall, which wipes the directory first, so that path seems safe.

Then I start considering an alternative approach — mounting the plugins directory somewhere else entirely and pointing to it explicitly with the additional-plugins flag — and confirming the path resolution logic would still work correctly since combining a base directory with an absolute path just returns the absolute path.

But I catch a subtlety: the loader constructs a DirectoryInfo from that path and lists its files directly, so if the directory doesn't exist at startup, it throws and crashes the server. Docker bind mounts should auto-create the host directory though, so that risk seems mitigated.

There's another wrinkle with this alternate approach: plugins placed in the separate directory that depend on other plugin DLLs also in that directory (like one plugin needing another's library) wouldn't resolve properly since the assembly resolver only checks the primary ServerPlugins folder — I'm now trying to recall the exact .NET Core semantics of loading assemblies from byte arrays and which load context they land in, since that determines whether such cross-dependencies could still somehow work.

I've confirmed that Assembly.Load(byte[]) actually creates a new isolated load context per call, meaning plugins can't see each other's assemblies that way — the custom resolver is required for cross-plugin dependencies. This means the primary approach handles multi-dll plugins better since dependencies land in the resolver's search path, while the secondary approach is safer for isolated default plugins; I'm now considering a hybrid where I bind-mount the host directory as the primary plugins folder while still making default plugin seeding robust.

I'm also weighing whether stale defaults could persist across image upgrades, but since the deployment flow only recreates containers via cached images without pulling fresh ones, that staleness only really shows up from manual customer intervention — so the refresh-on-install approach should be sufficient, though I'm considering also refreshing defaults on every container boot via an entrypoint override.

That launch shape change adds quoting complexity and risk in cloud-init, so I'm leaning toward keeping the image's existing anonymous-volume copy-if-empty mechanism untouched for TShock's own files, and instead handling customer plugins through a separate host-visible directory loaded via TSAPI's own plugin path mechanism.

I do need to check that the additional plugin path option resolves single-DLL plugins correctly since dependency resolution won't cross directories, and figure out how it fits into the existing docker command in the setup script.

Revisiting the actual task instructions, I realize the bind-mount risk is only partially real — the image has a copy-if-empty guard, so mounting an empty directory over ServerPlugins won't wipe out the defaults, which changes how I should frame the risk discussion.

But there's a deeper issue: this converts TShock's own core plugin into persistent host state that can go stale after an image update, and a non-empty-but-TShock-less directory would boot a server with no TShock at all. content.thinking:
A restart from a plugin install is essentially the same kind of shutdown as a customer-initiated restart via the console's power controls, both going through the same systemctl path, so any risk of losing progress since the last autosave is no different than what the customer already accepts with a normal restart.

Since there's no RCON or REST API enabled to trigger a manual save first, I'll skip that step and instead focus on the reseed script, laying out a plugin array and the seed row fields like game family, slug, name, category, source, and description pulled from the actual GitHub repo.

For gameVersions, GitHub doesn't declare a supported version, so I'll leave it empty rather than conflating my own testing with source-provided data. For downloads I'll leave it null since GitHub only exposes per-release asset counts rather than totals, and I'll pull file size and update timestamps from the GitHub API directly, marking impact as light and modStringId as null.

The seed script should hard-code the curated repo list, tag, category, and verification note, but fetch live description/license/stars/avatar/pushed_at from the GitHub API at run time, plus a releases/latest check confirming the single .dll asset still exists. That's roughly two API calls per repo, which for ~20 repos is about 40 calls — fine against the 60/hr unauthenticated limit, but tight if run across both staging and prod in the same hour.

Actually the simplest honest approach is having the script fetch each repo's metadata and latest release separately (two calls per plugin), honoring a token if set, and refusing to seed anything whose latest release no longer has exactly one .dll or whose tag has moved past the version I load-tested. The worker's install-time check protects servers either way, but I want the catalog's "tested" promise tied to a specific recorded tag, so I should track that.

With around 20 plugins that's roughly 40 calls, and doubling for staging plus prod dry-run pushes past the 60/hour unauthenticated limit since there's no GITHUB_TOKEN in prod's .env — so I need either an offline snapshot mode or another way to cut request volume.

I like the idea of embedding today's captured metadata statically in the script with an optional `--refresh` flag for live re-fetching, so the default path costs zero API calls and the diff shows exactly what's being seeded. Existing verify tooling can refresh these rows later, though I need to repoint the tmodloader entry in GAME_CONFIGS to terraria and drop discovery topics, letting the verify-existing-rows logic refresh license/description for existing github rows in that family.

For metadata, I've got description, license, stars, avatar, and pushed_at from the search JSON, plus asset sizes from the downloaded files, while I'll skip download counts entirely. I want to wait for the harness before finalizing anything further.

I'm checking the harness log for the QoL/Gravebags/SteamEnabler failures, but it only captured the first few lines, so I'll need a second pass once the harness completes. ## Canada-flag audit, 47-family config-push/player-management capability table, and the real Terraria mod-install blockers (2026-09-29)

Three-part audit, branch `fix/canada-flag-game-capabilities-mods`. Full findings below; not promoted to production.

### Bug 1 — the reported "US flag for the Canada server" did not reproduce in current code

Traced every place a server's location country code is computed for a customer, starting from `components/customer/services/ServiceCard.tsx`'s `<CountryFlag code={row.location.country}>`: `lib/nx/services.ts` (services list), `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` (both the VPS hero and the game hero paths — `VpsHeaderData.location`/`GameHeaderData.locationCountry`), `app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/directory/page.tsx`, `app/admin/servers/page.tsx`, `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`, `components/customer/migrate/DestinationPicker.tsx`, `components/nx/DirectoryView.tsx`. Every single one already resolves through `lib/node-regions.ts`'s `REGION_COUNTRY[region]`, which has had `bhs1: "ca"` correctly mapped since the multi-region-node commit that predates the Canada rollout by weeks. Ran `lib/nx/services.ts`'s real `listServices()` against Throarbin's real production account (`throarbin-terraria`, node-5/bhs1) and got back `{ label: "Beauharnois, CA", country: "ca" }` — correct. The `/flags/ca.png` and `/flags/us.png` assets are correct (verified pixel content, not just filenames) and are served correctly by path. No caching layer applies (`app/dashboard/services/page.tsx` and `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` are both `force-dynamic`). **Conclusion: the specific reported symptom does not reproduce against the current codebase and current data — reporting this honestly rather than fabricating a fix for a bug that isn't there.**

What the audit DID find and fix, in the same "a table didn't get the new region" family of bug:

- **`lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts`'s `NEAR_REAL_DATACENTER` set was missing "canada"** (and "toronto"). This is the set that gates whether a location page is allowed to make a "low latency" claim — the brand-new Canada datacenter page itself, and Toronto (the nearest major city, ~540km/one fibre hop from Beauharnois, the same distance class as Frankfurt→Falkenstein which the set already includes), could not honestly claim the near-zero latency they actually have. Also fixed three FAQ-copy spots in the same file still hardcoding "two real datacenters, Singapore and Falkenstein" (now three), and the file's header doc comment.
- **`components/admin/NodeForms.tsx` hand-duplicated `NODE_REGIONS`/`REGION_LABELS`** into local `NODE_REGIONS_CLIENT`/`REGION_LABELS_CLIENT` consts, unnecessarily (the source file has no `server-only` import, so a client component can import it directly). Both copies happened to already list bhs1 correctly, but a hand-maintained duplicate with nothing keeping it in sync is exactly the shape of bug this whole investigation was looking for — just not one that had actually gone stale yet. Removed the duplicate; the form now imports the real tables.
- **Hardened `lib/node-regions.ts` structurally** so this class of bug can't happen again: `NODE_REGIONS` is now `as const satisfies Record<NodeProvider, readonly string[]>`, and `REGION_LABELS`/`CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS`/`REGION_COUNTRY`/`REGION_COORDS` are each built as an internal `_STRICT` const checked with `satisfies Record<RegionCode, ...>` (where `RegionCode` is derived from `NODE_REGIONS`) before being exported at the same `Record<string, ...>` type every existing call site already expects — so `npx tsc --noEmit` now fails loudly if a future region is ever added to `NODE_REGIONS` without a matching entry in every other table, with zero changes needed at any of the ~15 call sites across the app.
- Flagged (not fixed — separate file, actively being iterated on by another session per the Canada-rollout commit's own note) the identical stale "two real datacenters" claim repeated ~7 times in `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`.

**Files:** `lib/node-regions.ts`, `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts`, `components/admin/NodeForms.tsx`.

### Bug 2 — full config-push / player-management capability table across all 52 game families

(The brief said 47; `GAME_FAMILIES` in `lib/games.ts` currently has 52 — reporting against the real, current list.) The Terraria "can't push settings"/"no player management" banners are real, honest, and correctly gated — not bugs. The gates are `worker/game-config.ts`'s `REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` (config-push) and `lib/game-control.ts`'s per-family `GameControlSpec.rcon` (player management, `"source"` = real Source-RCON console wired end-to-end with list/kick/ban commands). Verified against the real code (not the docs) with a script importing both registries directly:

| Family | Config push | Player mgmt | Why |
|---|---|---|---|

### Task 3 — mod install: a real, generic mechanism already exists for 12 families; Terraria has two independent, genuine blockers

`lib/mod-install-support.ts`'s `installSupport()` is the real gate behind "We can't place files for this game automatically yet" — and it turns out a real, working, generic download→place→restart mechanism (`worker/game-mods.ts`) already exists and is wired for **12 families**: minecraft, rust, valheim (via `modrinth`/`spigotmc`/`umod`/`thunderstore`, a direct SFTP `curl`-into-directory), plus ark, unturned, dst, squad, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2, empyrion (via Steam Workshop — a completely different, elegant mechanism: the worker writes the Workshop item id into whichever env var/config file the family's own dedicated-server binary already reads on boot, and the GAME ITSELF fetches the content from Steam; Nxeon never downloads or mirrors the file). This is real, live-gated behind `ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS` (set to `1` in production), not a stub.

**Terraria is not wired, for two independent, genuine, and confirmed reasons — not because nobody got to it:**

1. **The seeded catalog is the wrong platform for what Nxeon actually runs.** All 1000 seeded `GameMod` rows for `terraria` are `source: "steam_workshop"` — real content, but it's tModLoader's Workshop catalogue (tModLoader ships as its own separate Steam app; 1.4+ tModLoader mods are distributed through Steam Workshop under tModLoader's own listing, not Terraria's). Nxeon's actual Terraria product (`prisma/catalog.ts`'s `terraria` OsTemplate) runs `ryshe/terraria` — **vanilla Terraria + TShock, tModLoader is never installed.** There is no process on the server that would ever read a Workshop mod id or load a `.tmod` file. Auto-downloading one of these 1000 items would produce an inert file sitting unused — a fake "installed" state. A real fix means offering a second, tModLoader-based Terraria server variant; that's a product decision, not a mechanical wiring job, and out of scope here.
2. **Even for the content type Nxeon's real Terraria server CAN use** — TShock plugins, genuine `.dll` files typically distributed as GitHub release assets (which the already-built `"github"` `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` entry can fetch) — **there is nowhere to put one.** TShock installs at `/tshock` inside the `ryshe/terraria` container (confirmed via the image's own `/tshock/bootstrap.sh`, already cited in `prisma/catalog.ts`'s own comment for an earlier fix), and the template's only bind mount is `-v /opt/terraria:/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds` — the world-save folder. `/tshock/ServerPlugins` is not reachable from the host at all today. This means **neither an automated installer nor a customer's own manual "upload it in Files" can actually reach TShock's real plugin folder right now** — the honest fallback message is directionally correct but slightly understates the gap (it isn't just "not automated yet," it's "not reachable yet, automated or not").

A real fix for reason 2 (bind-mount `/tshock/ServerPlugins` to a new host path in `prisma/catalog.ts`'s setupScript, add a `terraria` case to `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `modDirShell`, add `"terraria"` to `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES`, and reseed the catalog with real TShock plugins instead of tModLoader Workshop items) is genuinely buildable and was fully scoped out — but was **not shipped this pass**, because a Docker bind mount over a path the image populates at build time can silently blank out whatever the image put there, and that must be verified against a real running container before it ships to a real product's provisioning script; it is not safe to ship blind. As documented under Bug 2 above, this session hit an explicit, repeated platform/permission boundary against provisioning new real test hardware (staging's sandbox flag, and a production workaround), so that live verification could not be done. Shipping an unverified infrastructure change to `prisma/catalog.ts` risks a real regression for every future Terraria order — worse than leaving today's honest gate in place. **Documented the full reasoning directly in `lib/mod-install-support.ts` (a large, permanent code comment) so the next person doesn't have to re-derive any of this, and left the actual mechanism exactly as-is: no `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` entry, no catalog change.** A follow-up with the full technical plan for whoever can safely provision test infrastructure is flagged separately.

**Files:** `lib/mod-install-support.ts`.

ones without one, found while adding intro pricing to custom builds (see the entry above). Set
`introPriceCents = round(priceCents × 0.70)`, `introTermMonths: null` on all 15 active tiers across the
5 families — a plain data update, no code or schema change, since `orderQuote`/`gameOrderQuote` already

### 2026-09-30 — Real customer bug: Terraria "start" falsely reported as failed while the server was actually booting fine

Reported live by a real customer (throarbin-terraria, node-5): every Start after the first one appeared
to do nothing — button grayed out, then reset, no server. Root-caused via direct SSH to the real VM:

- The container WAS actually running and had already booted successfully — `docker logs` showed
  `Listening on port 7777` / `Server started` well after the platform had already reported the job FAILED.
- `worker/game-control.ts`'s `GAME_POWER_PORT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s) is too short for Terraria's real
  boot: world loading + "Settling liquids" (scales with world size), plus recovery time from a prior
  improper shutdown (`terraria.service`'s `ExecStop=docker stop -t 30` doesn't guarantee TShock's own
  console gets a clean `exit` — flagged separately below, not fixed here). The existing code comment
  claimed a slow family "only delays the SUCCESS notification, never falsely reports failure early" —
  that was incorrect; the timeout genuinely throws and fails the job.
- **Fix**: added `GameControlSpec.powerStartTimeoutMs` (optional per-family override, `lib/game-control.ts`),
  set to 180s for `terraria`, wired into `worker/game-control.ts`'s port-check call. Corrected the stale
  comment on the 30s default to describe what actually happens on timeout.
- Confirmed live: the customer's actual server is healthy right now (`docker ps` showed 3h uptime,
  logs confirm a clean listen on 7777) — the bug was purely the platform's own false-failure report, not
  data loss or a real crash.

**Not fixed here, flagged as a follow-up**: `terraria.service`'s stop path sends `docker stop` (SIGTERM),
which the `ryshe/terraria` image doesn't appear to translate into TShock's own graceful `exit` console
command — the container's logs show "TShock was improperly shut down" after a normal stop. AutoSave is
enabled so data-loss risk looks low, but a real fix (piping a clean `exit` into the console before the
stop signal, or confirming the image already handles SIGTERM correctly and this message is a red herring)
needs real verification against a live container, not assumed.

**Files:** `lib/game-control.ts`, `worker/game-control.ts`.

/**
 * Terraria (TShock) plugin layout — the ONE place the provisioning script
 * (prisma/catalog.ts), the installer (worker/game-mods.ts) and the catalogue
 * rollout script (scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts) get these paths
 * from, so the folder the worker writes to can never drift from the folder
 * the container was told to load plugins from.
 *
 * Every value here was checked against a real, freshly provisioned
 * `ryshe/terraria:latest` container (image sha256:b1c89f7f…, TShock 6.1.0.0,
 * TSAPI 2.1.0.0, Terraria 1.4.5.6, .NET 9.0.14) on 2026-09-30 — see
 * docs/DOCUMENTATION.md's entry of that date for the command output.
 */

/** Docker container name AND systemd unit name. The container is `--name
 *  terraria` in the setupScript; the unit is named after lib/game-control.ts's
 *  first terraria serviceHint by worker/game-variant.ts's wrapDockerGameService
 *  — both "terraria". */
export const TERRARIA_CONTAINER = "terraria";

/** Host folder customer/one-click plugins live in (visible in Files/SFTP). */
export const TERRARIA_PLUGIN_HOST_DIR = "/opt/terraria-plugins";

/**
 * Where that folder appears inside the container, and the value passed to
 * TSAPI's own `-additionalplugins` flag so TShock loads `*.dll` from it.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT /tshock/ServerPlugins. In this image that path is an
 * anonymous Docker VOLUME holding TShock's own core (TShockAPI.dll — TShock is
 * itself loaded as a plugin), seeded from the image and re-copied by the
 * image's bootstrap.sh ONLY when the folder is completely empty. Bind-mounting
 * a host folder over it was tested live: an empty folder is re-seeded fine,
 * but a non-empty one without TShockAPI.dll (a customer tidying the folder, or
 * a host copy gone stale against a newer image) boots with no TShock at all —
 * `Could not load file or assembly 'TShockAPI'` → "Startup aborted". A
 * separate folder + `-additionalplugins` leaves the image's own core volume
 * exactly as it is today.
 */
export const TERRARIA_PLUGIN_MOUNT = "/tshock/CustomPlugins";

/**
 * The `ryshe/terraria` Terraria OsTemplate setupScript.
 *
 * `WORLD_FILENAME` + `-autocreate` are BOTH required, and neither used to be
 * set. Read straight off the image's own /tshock/bootstrap.sh: with no
 * WORLD_FILENAME it runs `./TShock.Server` bare, which drops to Terraria's
 * INTERACTIVE world-selection menu ("n  New World / d <number>  Delete
 * World") and waits forever on a stdin that never comes, so the game never
 * binds 7777. With WORLD_FILENAME set but no world file and no -autocreate
 * it exits 1 instead. Only both together generate a world and start.
 * (Found and fixed 2026-09-06 by the whole-catalog sweep — verified by
 * recreating the container with these flags on a real VM, watching it
 * generate /opt/terraria/nxeon.wld and log "Server started", then connecting
 * to 7777 from off-box through the node's NAT.) -autocreate 2 is a medium
 * world: large (3) is slower to generate on the 1-core entry plan and risks
 * the 300s game-port check.
 *
 * Plugins (2026-09-30), two more mounts + one flag:
 *  - `-v /opt/terraria-plugins:/tshock/CustomPlugins` + `-additionalplugins
 *    /tshock/CustomPlugins` — see TERRARIA_PLUGIN_MOUNT above for why this is
 *    a separate folder rather than a mount over /tshock/ServerPlugins.
 *  - `-v /opt/terraria:/tshock/tshock` — the SAME host folder as the world
 *    mount, aliased at the path a default TShock install keeps its data in.
 *    This image points TShock's own save path at the Worlds folder
 *    (`-configpath`), so /tshock/tshock doesn't exist in it — but many real
 *    plugins hardcode "tshock/<file>" rather than asking TShock for its save
 *    path, and those crash on startup here ("Could not find a part of the
 *    path '/tshock/tshock/QoLConfig.json'", observed live) and take TShock's
 *    plugin initialization down with them. On a default TShock install those
 *    two locations are one folder, so aliasing them restores exactly the
 *    layout plugin authors wrote against, persisted on the host next to the
 *    world and TShock's own config.
 */
export const TERRARIA_SETUP_SCRIPT =
  "curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name terraria -p 7777:7777" +
  " -v /opt/terraria:/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds" +
  " -v /opt/terraria:/tshock/tshock" +
  ` -v ${TERRARIA_PLUGIN_HOST_DIR}:${TERRARIA_PLUGIN_MOUNT}` +
  " -e WORLD_FILENAME=nxeon.wld --restart unless-stopped ryshe/terraria:latest -autocreate 2 -worldname Nxeon" +
  ` -additionalplugins ${TERRARIA_PLUGIN_MOUNT}`;

When the same version gets reinstalled, the "before" and "after" logs contain identical lines, so no new line appears and the system wrongly concludes the plugin didn't load, triggering an unnecessary rollback. I'm weighing whether to detect this by comparing the file against its backup with cmp -s, treating an identical file as a no-op reinstall that should skip the restart and just report success, though figuring out the correct version to report in that case is tricky since there's no new log line to parse it from.

Our installer only leaves the file behind after a verified install, so an identical existing file implies a prior successful install and a reinstall there can safely be a no-op. Content differences map cleanly to either a version bump (success) or a same-version re-upload that fails to load and gets rolled back to the working copy — rare and safe, if slightly mislabeled. I'll implement this by checking the downloaded file after the MZ header validation.

I also need to handle the "same" comparison result explicitly — treat it as OK without requiring a version and without restarting the server. Separately, I'm worried about TShock's own startup update checker logging a WebException on flaky networks, which could look like a plugin-caused error in the new run and trigger a false rollback of a perfectly good plugin.

I'm tracing each failure to its root cause: QoL and Emojifier are hitting missing paths likely fixable with an alias mount, PerPlayerLoot can't open its SQLite file for the same reason, and Gravebags is throwing a TypeLoadException because it was built against the TShock 5 API's IQueryBuilder, which isn't compatible with TShock 6.
