I'm refining my detection to only count lines that clearly indicate plugin-level crashes, like "has had an unhandl..."

A more precise signal is TSAPI's specific warning format for handler exceptions, which names the offending plugin directly and avoids false positives from internal try/catch logging like update checks. I can attribute each unhandled exception to the exact plugin by matching the plugin name extracted from its initiation line against the name in the exception warning, giving a much more reliable failure signal than a generic string search.

I'm working through the shell script logic to extract new plugin names, handle spaces in names, and safely check them against the log for unhandled exceptions—running into subshell variable scoping issues with the while loop and needing a temp-file-based approach instead of process substitution for portability.

Names with special characters are unlikely enough to not worry about. I should keep the new-run abort detection intact in nx_restart_wait, since this precise attribution approach avoids false positives from unrelated noise. There's also a timing consideration — GamePostInitialize handlers and exceptions like PerPlayerLoot's could occur before "Server started" is logged, but the sleep afterward should cover slight delays. content.thinking:
Running through the first pass without the alias mount, most plugins initialize fine without exceptions—ComfyEconomy, BossManager, PlaytimeRewards, and the rest of the list all load cleanly.

PerPlayerLoot throws a sqlite exception, while QoL, Gravebags, SteamEnabler, Emojifier, RankSystem, and Skynomi-Extension outright fail (the last needs its base plugin). A separate batch fails to download due to network issues—FACommands, Abilities, Bagger, BanGuard, and several others.

I'm now flagging plugins that could be risky for a hosting catalog: CheckBag periodically bans players based on inventory checks, which seems like something that could misfire on unsuspecting users, while SkipVersionCheck and MobileCrossplay just loosen client compatibility restrictions in ways that seem like reasonable admin options rather than dangers.

I want to curate a set of broadly useful, English-friendly plugins rather than dumping everything in — customers will actually see this list, so quality and clarity matter more than quantity, especially since the owner can always disable extras later. I'm sorting candidates into categories like economy (ComfyEconomy, PlaytimeRewards), admin/moderation (Inventory Viewer, Region Extension, TheObserver), and gameplay (BossManager, TerraJump, BridgeBuilder, loot chest plugins), weighing each for license availability, real functionality, and clear English documentation.

I still need to retest several MIT-licensed plugins that failed to load earlier (FACommands, Bagger, PvPer, DisableRevenge, Grace-Period, No-Teams, BanGuard) and a few others with alias/mount conflicts (QoL, Emojifier, PerPlayerLoot), while excluding ones like Gravebags that are incompatible with the current TShock API, plus flagging RankSystem and Skynomi-Extension for further review.

For the Chinese-only plugins (PlayerManager, WorldModify, ProgressPlugin, CheckBag, FishShop), I'm weighing whether to exclude them editorially since they'd confuse customers even though they load fine -- I'll leave them out but note they can be added back if wanted, since it's really the owner's call.

For unlicensed repos, per existing policy they're allowed as link-out-only with an upstream note, so I'm considering including Inventory Viewer, Region Extension, BossManager, and CustomItems, though BossEvolution's description feels too weak to justify inclusion.

Now I'm planning a second pass with the full production install/remove scripts against a broader candidate set of roughly 28 plugins, covering the 20 confirmed OK, the alias hypotheses, and download failures I still want to verify.

Since 30 plugins at roughly two minutes each for install/remove restarts would take about an hour, I'm looking for a shortcut: deleting the plugin file directly instead of running the full remove-and-restart cycle, then letting the next plugin's install restart double as the clean boot. The diff logic should still work since I'm only checking for the new plugin's initialization line appearing.

I'll still run the actual remove script occasionally to verify it works, and rollback failures will just cost an extra restart. DNS flakiness during curl retries might still cause install failures, but I'll see how that plays out.

For the actual test pass, step one is doing a full final-layout reinstall matching what gameReinstall does, then looping through the plugin installs one by one.

model ServerMod {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  serverId    String
  server      Server   @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  modId       String
  mod         GameMod  @relation(fields: [modId], references: [id])
  status      String   @default("INSTALLING") // INSTALLING | INSTALLED | FAILED | REMOVING | REMOVED
  version     String?
  error       String? // last failure detail, surfaced in the portal
  installedAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  @@unique([serverId, modId])
  @@index([serverId])
}
model Notification {
  id        String    @id @default(cuid())
  title     String
  body      String?
  href      String?
  readAt    DateTime?
  userId    String
  user      User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  createdAt DateTime  @default(now())
}

content.content:
subscriptions ≥ 25 — deliberately low relative to Modrinth's importer's four-figure floor, because
these catalogues are a completely different shape (Squad's whole real catalogue is ~301 items; a
four-figure floor would gut it, while L4D2's ~220k items is exactly what a floor exists to filter),
capped at 1,000 rows/family. `license` is always null (Workshop items never carry one) and
`category` is uniformly `"Workshop"` (Steam's API has no clean maps-vs-mods split to key off honestly).
Idempotent (`@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` upsert) — verified by running it twice.

**Real, verified import counts (production, 2026-09-20):** ark 1000, unturned 1000, dst 1000,
squad 272 (of 301 total — the whole real catalogue above the floor), empyrion 1000, soulmask 678 (of
700 total), projectzomboid 1000, tf2 1000, l4d2 1000, palworld 1000 (informational only, not
installable — see above). **8,950 real rows total, 0 failures.**

**Side finding, not caused by this work but hit while running it:** a concurrent agent worktree's
`node_modules` is symlinked to this tree's, and something regenerated the shared Prisma Client
against a schema with a `GameMod.longDescription` column this database doesn't have yet — any
default-shaped `GameMod` write throws "column does not exist." Worked around in the importer with an
explicit `select: { id: true }` rather than touching the shared client (a live agent may be mid-flight
on that migration). Flagged separately for a real fix — see the open task on production Prisma
client/DB drift.

**2. Install-time mechanism — `worker/game-mods.ts`'s new Steam Workshop section, `lib/mod-install-support.ts`.**
`INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` gained the 9 families above; `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` gained `steam_workshop`. Every
apply function recomputes the server's FULL desired Workshop-id set from its `ServerMod` rows each
time (`desiredWorkshopMods` + `workshopSync`) rather than patching one id in isolation, because most
of these mechanisms are one field holding the whole list. Per-family mechanism, and how confident it
is:

| Family | Mechanism | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| ark | `GAME_MOD_IDS` env var (comma), container recreate | **Verified** — matches both the ARK wiki's own `-mods=`/`ActiveMods=` docs AND `hermsi/ark-server`'s documented env var name exactly. |
| dst | `MODS` env var (comma), container recreate | **Verified** — matches both `dedicated_server_mods_setup.lua`'s real mechanism AND `yeetzone/dontstarvetogether`'s documented `MODS` env var exactly. |
| squad | `MODS` env var (`(id1 id2)`), container recreate | **Verified against the image** — `cm2network/squad`'s own docs give this exact format. The RAW dedicated binary actually needs a separate `steamcmd workshop_download_item` + manual placement step (confirmed via the Squad Wiki mod-upload page and community host docs), but this image wraps that internally, so from Nxeon's side it is genuinely a pure env-var write. |
| soulmask | `MOD_IDS` env var (comma), container recreate | **Image mechanism verified** (`indifferentbroccoli/soulmask-server-docker`'s README documents `MOD_IDS` exactly). The underlying game mechanism itself (`-mod=` launch arg) is best-available community evidence only — Soulmask's Workshop support is brand new and has no stable official dedicated-server doc yet. |
| unturned | Writes `Servers/nxeon/WorkshopDownloadConfig.json` directly (no restart triggered) | **Verified** — Smartly Dressed Games' own official server-hosting docs. Path is deterministic from this platform's fixed `SERVER_ID=nxeon` setup script. |
| projectzomboid | Writes `WorkshopItems=`/`Mods=` in `servertest.ini` | **Verified mechanism** (PZwiki), but PZ needs BOTH the numeric Workshop id and the mod's own internal string id, which the Workshop API never exposes. Solved with a one-time `steamcmd workshop_download_item` **inside the customer's own container**, reading `mod.info`, then deleting what was fetched immediately — nothing is kept or mirrored; the dedicated server re-fetches its own real copy on boot. Result is cached onto the `GameMod` row so it only runs once, ever, per mod. |
| tf2 | Appends `tf_workshop_map_sync <id>` lines to `tf/cfg/server.cfg` | **Mechanism confirmed** via the long-standing Valve-endorsed community guide (wiki.teamfortress.com has no Workshop page of its own — flagged as the best available source, not a Valve dev doc). **Gated honestly**: `cm2network/tf2` documents that Workshop maps need a real `SRCDS_WORKSHOP_AUTHKEY`, which Nxeon does not provision today — install fails with a clear message rather than writing a line that would silently never activate. |
23:**Entry points.** `GamePlan` model (`prisma/schema.prisma:777`) layers a game tier on a base `Plan`

### 2026-09-30 — One-click TShock plugins for Terraria, verified on a real provisioned server (branch `feature/terraria-real-mod-install`, NOT promoted)

Closes the two Terraria blockers from the 2026-09-29 entry above (Task 3). Everything below was checked
against a **real, brand-new Terraria server provisioned through the production worker** for this purpose
(`tmods-test-29d892`, node-2, owned by the internal user `terraria-modtest@nxeon-internal.test` — no
customer server was touched), not assumed. Image under test: `ryshe/terraria:latest`
sha256:b1c89f7f359a…, created 2026-03-11 — TShock 6.1.0.0, TerrariaAPI 2.1.0.0, Terraria 1.4.5.6,
.NET 9.0.14.

**What a stock container actually has (before any change).** `/tshock/ServerPlugins` is an *anonymous
Docker volume* (the image declares `VOLUME /tshock/ServerPlugins`) containing exactly `TShockAPI.dll`,
`.deps.json`, `.pdb`, `.xml` — TShock itself is loaded as a plugin from there
(`[Server API] Info Plugin TShock v6.1.0.0 (by The TShock Team) initiated.`). The image keeps a backup
copy at `/plugins` (identical sha256s), and its `bootstrap.sh` re-copies `/plugins/*` into ServerPlugins
**only when that folder is completely empty**.

**The bind-mount risk, tested rather than assumed — and why the scoped fix was changed.**
- Mounting an *empty* host folder over `/tshock/ServerPlugins` does NOT lose the defaults on first boot:
  bootstrap logs `Copying plugins...`, the host folder ends up with the same four files (same sha256s),
  TShock initiates. So the naive mount "works" on day one.
- But it turns TShock's own core into host state. Tested live: with that mount, a folder that is
  non-empty but missing `TShockAPI.dll` (a customer tidying the folder in Files; or a host copy left
  stale against a newer image — the copy-if-empty guard never refreshes it) boots with **no TShock at all**:
  `Could not load file or assembly 'TShockAPI, Version=5.2.0.0'` → `Startup aborted due to an exception
  in the Server API initialization`, and the world still comes up and logs `Server started`.
- So the risk is real, just not in the form first feared. **Handled by not mounting over ServerPlugins at
  all**: the setupScript bind-mounts a separate `/opt/terraria-plugins` at `/tshock/CustomPlugins` and
  passes TSAPI's own `-additionalplugins /tshock/CustomPlugins` flag (the flag's string is present in this
  build's `TerrariaServer.dll`; TSAPI's `LoadPlugins` scans those folders' top-level `*.dll` in addition to
  ServerPlugins). The image's core volume is untouched: after the change ServerPlugins still holds the same
  four files, owner `1001:1001`, image timestamps, identical sha256s.
- A third mount, `-v /opt/terraria:/tshock/tshock`, aliases the world/config folder at the path a default
  TShock install keeps its data in. This image points TShock's save path at the Worlds folder, so
  `/tshock/tshock` doesn't exist — and many plugins hardcode `tshock/<file>`. Observed live without the
  alias: QoL and Emojifier aborted startup with `Could not find a part of the path
  '/tshock/tshock/…Config.json'`; with it, Emojifier loads and its config lands in `/opt/terraria`.
  Verified the alias is the same directory (`stat` → same device:inode for both container paths).

**Final setupScript verified end to end** by running exactly what `GAME_REINSTALL` would run with it
(stop unit → `docker rm -f` → wipe both host folders → the worker's `buildGameSetupScript` output → unit
active) on the test VM: fresh world generated, `-additionalplugins` in the container's Cmd, both binds +
the untouched ServerPlugins volume present, TShock initiated, `Server started`, and the installer's own
folder probe resolved to `/opt/terraria-plugins`.

**Installer: restart, prove it loaded, or roll back** (`lib/terraria-plugins.ts` scripts + parsers,
`worker/game-mods.ts` orchestration). TShock only loads plugins at startup, and a broken plugin doesn't
just skip itself — it aborts TShock's plugin initialization for the whole server. So an install downloads
the author's own latest GitHub release asset (exactly one `.dll` required), checks it's a PE file, restarts
the `terraria` unit, and marks it INSTALLED only if TShock logged a *new*
`Plugin X vY (by Z) initiated.` line and no abort / no `Plugin "X" has had an unhandled exception`
naming that same plugin. Anything else: file removed (or the previous version restored), server
restarted again, ServerMod FAILED with TShock's own reason. The whole sequence runs as one detached
script on the VM, polled over short SSH sessions, so a dropped connection can't strand it between
"placed" and "verified". Removal deletes the file and restarts (if running) so "removed" is true of the
running server. A server that was stopped is started only to verify and stopped again. The folder is read
off the **live** container (mount + flag); a server provisioned before this change has neither and gets an
honest "set up before one-click Terraria plugins were available — contact support" instead of a fake
install. `installSupport` now also restricts terraria to the `github` source (new `FAMILY_SOURCES`), so
the old tModLoader Workshop rows can never show an Install button even before the reseed runs.

**Every catalogue plugin was installed on the real server by that production script** (31 attempted on
the final layout): 26 `RESULT:installed`, 5 correctly rolled back with `ROLLBACK:ok` — PerPlayerLoot and
QoL (`errors`: unhandled GamePostInitialize exception; QoL is `MissingFieldException 'Terraria.Main.rand'`,
a Terraria-1.4.4 build), PvPer, FloatingText-Chat, RankSystem (`bootfail`: exception during
initialization). The server came back clean after every rollback.

**Catalogue reseed** — `scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts` (dry run by default, `NXEON_DB_TARGET`
guarded): (1) updates only the `terraria` OsTemplate's setupScript (not a blanket `prisma/catalog.ts` run);
(2) retires every non-github terraria row — the 1000 tModLoader `steam_workshop` rows — deleting those
nothing references, deactivating any a ServerMod/ModRating still points at; (3) upserts 24 real TShock
plugins, each with its tested tag, real asset size, the TShock line it loaded as, and the repo's real
description/license/avatar. All 24 re-checked through the exact API call the worker makes
(`/repos/{repo}/releases/latest` → tag = tested tag, exactly one `.dll` asset, download 200 with the
API-reported size). Unlicensed repos are listed link-out-only with an `upstreamNote`, per
`scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`'s policy (the worker always downloads from the author's release).
Left out (tested, with reasons, in the script's `LEFT_OUT` block): the 5 rollbacks above; Gravebags
(TShock-5 `IQueryBuilder`), SteamEnablerPlugin, Skynomi-Extension, Abilities (a library);
TShock_RegionsKLP ("GSKLP purposes only" per its author); four Chinese-only plugins that loaded fine.

| Category | Plugins (all loaded on TShock 6.1.0.0) |
|---|---|
| Economy | ComfyEconomy, PlaytimeRewards |
| Admin | FACommands, Inventory Viewer, Region Extension, BanGuard, CustomItems, journeyUnlock, BossManager |
| Anti-cheat | The Observer |
| Gameplay | Bagger, TerraJump, IndividualLootChests (TSLootChest), Boss Evolution, Tradekey |
| PvP / Minigames | Grace Period, No Teams, Pinger |
| Chat | Emojifier, Show Armors |
| Quality of Life | BridgeBuilder, DisableRevenge |
| Compatibility | SkipVersionCheck, MobileCrossplay |

Importers stopped from re-adding the wrong platform: `scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts` no longer
has `terraria: 1281930` (tModLoader's appid); `scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`'s `tmodloader` config is
now a verify-only `terraria` entry (no discovery topics — an untested plugin can abort TShock's startup).
`lib/game-mods.ts`'s public mods-page copy said Terraria's platform was "tModLoader" — corrected to TShock
plugins, with the one-click installer named explicitly as that file's own rule requires.

**Rollout order (owner, at promote time):** run the reseed script against `nxeon` (applies all three data
steps), then promote the code. Either order is safe — code without data shows no Terraria Install buttons
(no github rows yet); data without code only changes new Terraria orders' container flags.

**Existing Terraria servers (2 live customers today: `terraria-i2ydef`, `throarbin-terraria`) are NOT
migrated** — their containers keep the old flags, so they get the honest "contact support" message.
Enabling one = recreate its container with the new mounts + flag, keeping `/opt/terraria` (world, TShock
config and users all live there, so they survive). Deliberately left as a per-server owner decision.

**Known gaps, not fixed here:** a Wipe & reinstall clears `/opt/terraria-plugins` but leaves ServerMod
rows saying INSTALLED — the same pre-existing gap every file-drop family has (Minecraft's plugins folder
is wiped the same way). A rolled-back plugin's config file (e.g. `QoLConfig.json`) stays in
`/opt/terraria`. Installs restart the server (players are kicked; TShock's AutoSave governs what's saved —
see the improper-shutdown follow-up in the entry above).

**Files:** `lib/terraria-plugins.ts` (new), `lib/mod-install-support.ts`, `worker/game-mods.ts`,
`prisma/catalog.ts`, `scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts` (new),
`scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`, `lib/game-mods.ts`,
`app/nxm/_data/mods-lib.ts`, `test/terraria-plugins.test.ts` (new).

I'm tracing the shutdown sequence: systemd stopped the unit, docker waited 30s before killing it since TShock ignores SIGTERM, and the unit ended up marked failed with exit code 137. That raises the question of why `systemctl restart` didn't actually start it back up afterward.

Actually, the pass2 script did finish and printed "NXTP:REMOVED" but never "NXTP:BOOT:...", meaning the remove script's is-active check found the service not active at that point. That points to the No-Teams install script, which stops the server if it wasn't already active before its own restart — so I need to figure out what state the unit was in right before that install ran.

The timing lines up: sleep 3 after "Server started" then the check for "was" active runs the stop. So "was" wasn't active for No-Teams' install, meaning some prior install left the server stopped, and that state cascaded forward. I need to trace back further to find which install first left the service non-active.

I should search the journal for "Started terraria.service" and "Stopped" pairs to trace exactly where the state transitioned to stopped.

I'm tracing the pattern now: each install stops the server if it wasn't active before, then the next install's restart logic starts it fresh from that stopped state—meaning every install sees "was != active" simply because the prior install left it stopped. I'm now wondering what caused this chain to begin in the first place.

Tracing back to the very first install, PerPlayerLoot started right after the final-layout setup which left the unit active, so its restart cycle should've ended active too — meaning the "was != active" stop must trigger somewhere later. The real question is whether a SIGKILL-terminated stop leaves the unit reporting "failed" on the next is-active check, which would explain the cascading stops across subsequent installs.

I notice the 5-second gap between "Stopped" and "Started" matches RestartSec exactly, which makes me suspect this restart actually came from systemd's automatic Restart=always mechanism rather than the manual `systemctl restart` command itself, since a manual restart shouldn't wait that interval.

Early on, the pattern is all normal restarts: TShock ignores SIGTERM, docker waits 30s then SIGKILLs (137), and the service restarts immediately after—no actual "was-stopped" events in this phase. I need to check the later window around 01:35 for anything different.

Later on, though, I see a different pattern: "Server started" followed a few seconds later by "Stopping," then "Stopped," then "Started" again—this looks like the next install script's restart chained right after the previous one finished booting. But at 01:49:22 there's a Stopping that follows Server started, then Stopped at 01:49:52 with a 137 failure, and critically no subsequent Started—meaning the final restart never actually brought the server back up, and the remove script's output is missing the expected boot confirmation line.

Re-checking the remove script logic, it only restarts if the service was active at check time, and it printed no boot line—so the Stopping at 01:49:22 must have come from a different install's "was not active" branch which just stops rather than restarts. That means the actual restart-and-start was left to whichever subsequent install script ran the restart-wait logic, explaining the gaps between Stopped and Started timestamps.

I need to trace back further to find when the state first flipped from active to not-active, so I should look at what happened around 01:25-01:36, possibly tied to a bootfail/rollback sequence for PvPer near 01:27.

BanGuard fails its API key validation and shuts the server down with exit 0, which systemd interprets as a clean exit and restarts—creating a loop. Looking at restart counter 5, the server actually got as far as "Server started" before BanGuard's slower check caught up and killed it seconds later, unlike earlier attempts that failed almost instantly, which explains why our detection logic mistakenly reported it as "installed."

I realize the real bug: nx_restart_wait reads logs since the first restart's StartedAt using docker's --since, so it captures output from all later restarts too, meaning it can see "Server started" from restart #5 even though the container is still crash-looping. The fix needs to verify stability after seeing "Server started" — confirm the container's current StartedAt still matches the observed run, wait a stability window, then recheck that no new restart occurred; if StartedAt changes again mid-poll, that should be flagged as the server restarting itself and treated as a failure.

Writing shell commands...

I'll combine the running-state and timestamp check into a single condition so a failure catches both "still exited" and "restarted but different timestamp" cases. For the failure reason, I want to surface something more useful than a generic message, so I'm thinking of tagging self-exits with a distinct marker and pulling the last meaningful log line before the crash as the explanation.

For the actual WHY extraction, I'm scoping the log grep to just the failed run's window and filtering for lines that look like errors or exceptions, while excluding known noise like the standard "Error Logging Enabled" message — that way something like the BanGuard API key validation error would surface as the real cause. I also want to account for exit failures triggering a rollback-and-retry loop, and make sure systemd states like activating/reloading still count as "running" for these checks, plus watch for crashes that happen after startup completes, like during a player join.

BanGuard should just be excluded from the seed list entirely since it requires an API key to function and shuts the server down without one — even with rollback protection, it would always fail on a fresh install, so there's no point listing it; I'll note it as left out. That raises a bigger concern though: other seed-list plugins verified during the cascade pass may have only passed because verification happened right after "Server started" with just a short stability window, meaning a plugin that crashes a bit later could've slipped through undetected — so I may need to redo verification with a longer stability window across the whole seed list, which is costly time-wise, so I'm looking for a shortcut.

Checking the journals themselves might let me confirm whether any plugin's container self-exited after that short window before the next stop was issued — from what I've seen, BanGuard is the only one showing that signature during the cascade pass, but a delayed exit past the window could still be hidden by our own stop command. The safest fix is rerunning the seed list with the corrected script and proper stability window, ideally on the more reliable server to sidestep flaky networking, and I could kick that run off in the background now since it only depends on SSH for control, not downloads.

Before doing that though, I realize server 1's unit is currently stopped, and if the install script treats "stopped" as its baseline state, it will restart and then re-stop the server after each verification — better to start the server first so it stays active and the install loop doesn't cycle it unnecessarily. The driver's cleanup step between installs should still work fine since a fresh install naturally unloads the prior one. Now I need to go fix the shell library itself.

p='lib/terraria-plugins.ts'
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index('/** Shell helpers shared by install + remove.'):s.index('/**\n * The detached install script for one plugin file.')]
new='''/** Shell helpers shared by install + remove.
 *
 * `nx_restart_wait` restarts the unit, waits for a NEW container run
 * (StartedAt changes), then waits for TShock's own "Server started" —
 * checking the abort markers FIRST, because (observed live) TSAPI still logs
 * "Server started" after aborting plugin initialization. It then holds for
 * NX_SETTLE seconds and requires the SAME run to still be up: observed live,
 * a plugin can shut the whole server down on its own shortly after start
 * (BanGuard with no API key: "Error validating BanGuard API key" → exit →
 * systemd's Restart=always → crash loop), and one of those restarts reached
 * "Server started" before exiting again. A run that exits or gets replaced
 * at any point is a failure. Prints "<ok|fail|exited|timeout> <startedAt|->".
 *
 * `nx_running` — was the customer's server meant to be up? systemd reports
 * "activating" while a Restart=always restart is pending, so that counts as
 * up; a deliberate stop shows "inactive", or "failed" (TShock ignores
 * SIGTERM, so `docker stop -t 30` ends in SIGKILL/137 — observed live). */
const SHELL_LIB = [
  `NX_SETTLE=20`,
  `nx_started() { docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER} 2>/dev/null; }`,
  `nx_state() { docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}} {{.State.StartedAt}}' ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER} 2>/dev/null; }`,
  `nx_runlog() { [ -n "$1" ] && [ "$1" != "-" ] && docker logs --since "$1" ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER} 2>&1; }`,
  `nx_running() { case "$(systemctl is-active ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER} 2>/dev/null)" in active|activating|reloading) return 0;; *) return 1;; esac; }`,
  `nx_restart_wait() {`,
  `  old=$(nx_started); systemctl restart ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER} >/dev/null 2>&1`,
  `  new="$old"; i=0`,
  `  while [ $i -lt 30 ]; do new=$(nx_started); [ -n "$new" ] && [ "$new" != "$old" ] && break; sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done`,
  `  if [ -z "$new" ] || [ "$new" = "$old" ]; then echo "timeout -"; return; fi`,
  `  i=0`,
  `  while [ $i -lt 80 ]; do`,
  `    [ "$(nx_state)" = "true $new" ] || { echo "exited $new"; return; }`,
  `    l=$(nx_runlog "$new")`,
  `    if printf '%s\\n' "$l" | grep -q -E 'Startup aborted|Failed to load assembly|has thrown an exception during initialization'; then echo "fail $new"; return; fi`,
  `    if printf '%s\\n' "$l" | grep -q 'Server started'; then`,
  `      sleep $NX_SETTLE`,
  `      if [ "$(nx_state)" = "true $new" ]; then echo "ok $new"; else echo "exited $new"; fi`,
  `      return`,
  `    fi`,
  `    sleep 3; i=$((i+1))`,
  `  done`,
  `  echo "timeout $new"`,
  `}`,
].join("\\n");

s=s.replace(old,new)

s=s.replace("""    `was=$(systemctl is-active ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER})`,""","""    `if nx_running; then was=up; else was=down; fi`,""")
s=s.replace("""    `  res=bootfail`,
    `  nx_runlog "$ts" | grep -E -m1 'Could not load file or assembly|Could not load type|Could not find a part of the path|Failed to load assembly|has thrown an exception during initialization' | sed 's/^/NXTP:WHY:/'`,""","""    `  res=bootfail; [ "$st" = exited ] && res=exited`,
    `  nx_runlog "$ts" | grep -E -m1 'Could not load file or assembly|Could not load type|Could not find a part of the path|Failed to load assembly|has thrown an exception during initialization' | sed 's/^/NXTP:WHY:/'`,
    // A self-shutdown usually says why just before it goes (e.g. BanGuard's
    // "Error validating BanGuard API key. Please check your configuration.").
    `  [ "$st" = exited ] && nx_runlog "$ts" | grep -i -E 'error|exception|fail|invalid' | grep -v -E 'Error Logging Enabled|improperly shut down' | tail -1 | sed 's/^/NXTP:WHY:/'`,""")
s=s.replace("""    `[ "$was" != active ] && systemctl stop ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER} >/dev/null 2>&1`,""","""    `[ "$was" = down ] && systemctl stop ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER} >/dev/null 2>&1`,""")
s=s.replace("""    `  if [ "$(systemctl is-active ${TERRARIA_CONTAINER})" = active ]; then set -- $(nx_restart_wait); echo "NXTP:BOOT:$1"; fi`,""","""    `  if nx_running; then set -- $(nx_restart_wait); echo "NXTP:BOOT:$1"; fi`,""")
# markers doc
s=s.replace(""" *   NXTP:BOOT:<ok|fail|timeout>  NXTP:NEW:<TShock's "Plugin … initiated." line>
 *   NXTP:WHY:<TShock's own error line>  NXTP:ROLLBACK:<ok|fail|timeout>
 *   NXTP:RESULT:<installed|same|noload|errors|bootfail>   NXTP:END""",""" *   NXTP:BOOT:<ok|fail|exited|timeout>  NXTP:NEW:<TShock's "Plugin … initiated." line>
 *   NXTP:WHY:<TShock's own error line>  NXTP:ROLLBACK:<ok|fail|exited|timeout>
 *   NXTP:RESULT:<installed|same|noload|errors|bootfail|exited>   NXTP:END""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

13855:> `/tshock/ServerPlugins`" was the wrong fix. See "2026-09-30 — One-click TShock plugins for Terraria" at
14155:### 2026-09-30 — One-click TShock plugins for Terraria, verified on a real provisioned server (branch `feature/terraria-real-mod-install`, NOT promoted)

14155	### 2026-09-30 — One-click TShock plugins for Terraria, verified on a real provisioned server (branch `feature/terraria-real-mod-install`, NOT promoted)
14156	
14157	Closes the two Terraria blockers from the 2026-09-29 entry above (Task 3). Everything below was checked
14158	against a **real, brand-new Terraria server provisioned through the production worker** for this purpose
14159	(`tmods-test-29d892`, node-2, owned by the internal user `terraria-modtest@nxeon-internal.test` — no
14160	customer server was touched), not assumed. Image under test: `ryshe/terraria:latest`
14161	sha256:b1c89f7f359a…, created 2026-03-11 — TShock 6.1.0.0, TerrariaAPI 2.1.0.0, Terraria 1.4.5.6,
14162	.NET 9.0.14.
14163	
14164	**What a stock container actually has (before any change).** `/tshock/ServerPlugins` is an *anonymous
14165	Docker volume* (the image declares `VOLUME /tshock/ServerPlugins`) containing exactly `TShockAPI.dll`,
14166	`.deps.json`, `.pdb`, `.xml` — TShock itself is loaded as a plugin from there
14167	(`[Server API] Info Plugin TShock v6.1.0.0 (by The TShock Team) initiated.`). The image keeps a backup
14168	copy at `/plugins` (identical sha256s), and its `bootstrap.sh` re-copies `/plugins/*` into ServerPlugins
14169	**only when that folder is completely empty**.
14170	
14171	**The bind-mount risk, tested rather than assumed — and why the scoped fix was changed.**
14172	- Mounting an *empty* host folder over `/tshock/ServerPlugins` does NOT lose the defaults on first boot:
14173	  bootstrap logs `Copying plugins...`, the host folder ends up with the same four files (same sha256s),
14174	  TShock initiates. So the naive mount "works" on day one.
14175	- But it turns TShock's own core into host state. Tested live: with that mount, a folder that is
14176	  non-empty but missing `TShockAPI.dll` (a customer tidying the folder in Files; or a host copy left
14177	  stale against a newer image — the copy-if-empty guard never refreshes it) boots with **no TShock at all**:
14178	  `Could not load file or assembly 'TShockAPI, Version=5.2.0.0'` → `Startup aborted due to an exception
14179	  in the Server API initialization`, and the world still comes up and logs `Server started`.
14180	- So the risk is real, just not in the form first feared. **Handled by not mounting over ServerPlugins at
14181	  all**: the setupScript bind-mounts a separate `/opt/terraria-plugins` at `/tshock/CustomPlugins` and
14182	  passes TSAPI's own `-additionalplugins /tshock/CustomPlugins` flag (the flag's string is present in this
14183	  build's `TerrariaServer.dll`; TSAPI's `LoadPlugins` scans those folders' top-level `*.dll` in addition to
14184	  ServerPlugins). The image's core volume is untouched: after the change ServerPlugins still holds the same
14185	  four files, owner `1001:1001`, image timestamps, identical sha256s.
14186	- A third mount, `-v /opt/terraria:/tshock/tshock`, aliases the world/config folder at the path a default
14187	  TShock install keeps its data in. This image points TShock's save path at the Worlds folder, so
14188	  `/tshock/tshock` doesn't exist — and many plugins hardcode `tshock/<file>`. Observed live without the
14189	  alias: QoL and Emojifier aborted startup with `Could not find a part of the path
14190	  '/tshock/tshock/…Config.json'`; with it, Emojifier loads and its config lands in `/opt/terraria`.
14191	  Verified the alias is the same directory (`stat` → same device:inode for both container paths).
14192	
14193	**Final setupScript verified end to end** by running exactly what `GAME_REINSTALL` would run with it
14194	(stop unit → `docker rm -f` → wipe both host folders → the worker's `buildGameSetupScript` output → unit
14195	active) on the test VM: fresh world generated, `-additionalplugins` in the container's Cmd, both binds +
14196	the untouched ServerPlugins volume present, TShock initiated, `Server started`, and the installer's own
14197	folder probe resolved to `/opt/terraria-plugins`.
14198	
14199	**Installer: restart, prove it loaded, or roll back** (`lib/terraria-plugins.ts` scripts + parsers,
14200	`worker/game-mods.ts` orchestration). TShock only loads plugins at startup, and a broken plugin doesn't
14201	just skip itself — it aborts TShock's plugin initialization for the whole server. So an install downloads
14202	the author's own latest GitHub release asset (exactly one `.dll` required), checks it's a PE file, restarts
14203	the `terraria` unit, and marks it INSTALLED only if TShock logged a *new*
14204	`Plugin X vY (by Z) initiated.` line and no abort / no `Plugin "X" has had an unhandled exception`
14205	naming that same plugin. Anything else: file removed (or the previous version restored), server
14206	restarted again, ServerMod FAILED with TShock's own reason. The whole sequence runs as one detached
14207	script on the VM, polled over short SSH sessions, so a dropped connection can't strand it between
14208	"placed" and "verified". Removal deletes the file and restarts (if running) so "removed" is true of the
14209	running server. A server that was stopped is started only to verify and stopped again. The folder is read
14210	off the **live** container (mount + flag); a server provisioned before this change has neither and gets an
14211	honest "set up before one-click Terraria plugins were available — contact support" instead of a fake
14212	install. `installSupport` now also restricts terraria to the `github` source (new `FAMILY_SOURCES`), so
14213	the old tModLoader Workshop rows can never show an Install button even before the reseed runs.
14214	
14215	**Every catalogue plugin was installed on the real server by that production script** (31 attempted on
14216	the final layout): 26 `RESULT:installed`, 5 correctly rolled back with `ROLLBACK:ok` — PerPlayerLoot and
14217	QoL (`errors`: unhandled GamePostInitialize exception; QoL is `MissingFieldException 'Terraria.Main.rand'`,
14218	a Terraria-1.4.4 build), PvPer, FloatingText-Chat, RankSystem (`bootfail`: exception during
14219	initialization). The server came back clean after every rollback.
14220	
14221	**Catalogue reseed** — `scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts` (dry run by default, `NXEON_DB_TARGET`
14222	guarded): (1) updates only the `terraria` OsTemplate's setupScript (not a blanket `prisma/catalog.ts` run);
14223	(2) retires every non-github terraria row — the 1000 tModLoader `steam_workshop` rows — deleting those
14224	nothing references, deactivating any a ServerMod/ModRating still points at; (3) upserts 24 real TShock
14225	plugins, each with its tested tag, real asset size, the TShock line it loaded as, and the repo's real
14226	description/license/avatar. All 24 re-checked through the exact API call the worker makes
14227	(`/repos/{repo}/releases/latest` → tag = tested tag, exactly one `.dll` asset, download 200 with the
14228	API-reported size). Unlicensed repos are listed link-out-only with an `upstreamNote`, per
14229	`scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`'s policy (the worker always downloads from the author's release).
14230	Left out (tested, with reasons, in the script's `LEFT_OUT` block): the 5 rollbacks above; Gravebags
14231	(TShock-5 `IQueryBuilder`), SteamEnablerPlugin, Skynomi-Extension, Abilities (a library);
14232	TShock_RegionsKLP ("GSKLP purposes only" per its author); four Chinese-only plugins that loaded fine.
14233	
14234	| Category | Plugins (all loaded on TShock 6.1.0.0) |
14235	|---|---|
14236	| Economy | ComfyEconomy, PlaytimeRewards |
14237	| Admin | FACommands, Inventory Viewer, Region Extension, BanGuard, CustomItems, journeyUnlock, BossManager |
14238	| Anti-cheat | The Observer |
14239	| Gameplay | Bagger, TerraJump, IndividualLootChests (TSLootChest), Boss Evolution, Tradekey |
14240	| PvP / Minigames | Grace Period, No Teams, Pinger |
14241	| Chat | Emojifier, Show Armors |
14242	| Quality of Life | BridgeBuilder, DisableRevenge |
14243	| Compatibility | SkipVersionCheck, MobileCrossplay |
14244	
14245	Importers stopped from re-adding the wrong platform: `scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts` no longer
14246	has `terraria: 1281930` (tModLoader's appid); `scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`'s `tmodloader` config is
14247	now a verify-only `terraria` entry (no discovery topics — an untested plugin can abort TShock's startup).
14248	`lib/game-mods.ts`'s public mods-page copy said Terraria's platform was "tModLoader" — corrected to TShock
14249	plugins, with the one-click installer named explicitly as that file's own rule requires.
14250	
14251	**Rollout order (owner, at promote time):** run the reseed script against `nxeon` (applies all three data
14252	steps), then promote the code. Either order is safe — code without data shows no Terraria Install buttons
14253	(no github rows yet); data without code only changes new Terraria orders' container flags.
14254	
14255	**Existing Terraria servers (2 live customers today: `terraria-i2ydef`, `throarbin-terraria`) are NOT
14256	migrated** — their containers keep the old flags, so they get the honest "contact support" message.
14257	Enabling one = recreate its container with the new mounts + flag, keeping `/opt/terraria` (world, TShock
14258	config and users all live there, so they survive). Deliberately left as a per-server owner decision.
14259	
14260	**Known gaps, not fixed here:** a Wipe & reinstall clears `/opt/terraria-plugins` but leaves ServerMod
14261	rows saying INSTALLED — the same pre-existing gap every file-drop family has (Minecraft's plugins folder
14262	is wiped the same way). A rolled-back plugin's config file (e.g. `QoLConfig.json`) stays in
14263	`/opt/terraria`. Installs restart the server (players are kicked; TShock's AutoSave governs what's saved —
14264	see the improper-shutdown follow-up in the entry above).
14265	
14266	**Files:** `lib/terraria-plugins.ts` (new), `lib/mod-install-support.ts`, `worker/game-mods.ts`,
14267	`prisma/catalog.ts`, `scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts` (new),
14268	`scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`, `lib/game-mods.ts`,
14269	`app/nxm/_data/mods-lib.ts`, `test/terraria-plugins.test.ts` (new).
14270	
14271	---
14272	
14273	*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`
14274	(server migration).*

/**
 * Terraria (TShock) plugin layout — the ONE place the provisioning script
 * (prisma/catalog.ts), the installer (worker/game-mods.ts) and the catalogue
 * rollout script (scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts) get these paths
 * from, so the folder the worker writes to can never drift from the folder
 * the container was told to load plugins from.
 *
 * Every value here was checked against a real, freshly provisioned
 * `ryshe/terraria:latest` container (image sha256:b1c89f7f…, TShock 6.1.0.0,
 * TSAPI 2.1.0.0, Terraria 1.4.5.6, .NET 9.0.14) on 2026-09-30 — see
 * docs/DOCUMENTATION.md's entry of that date for the command output.
 */

/** Docker container name AND systemd unit name. The container is `--name
 *  terraria` in the setupScript; the unit is named after lib/game-control.ts's
 *  first terraria serviceHint by worker/game-variant.ts's wrapDockerGameService
 *  — both "terraria". */
export const TERRARIA_CONTAINER = "terraria";

/** Host folder customer/one-click plugins live in (visible in Files/SFTP). */
export const TERRARIA_PLUGIN_HOST_DIR = "/opt/terraria-plugins";

/**
 * Where that folder appears inside the container, and the value passed to
 * TSAPI's own `-additionalplugins` flag so TShock loads `*.dll` from it.
 *

 * image's bootstrap.sh ONLY when the folder is completely empty. Bind-mounting
 * a host folder over it was tested live: an empty folder is re-seeded fine,
 * but a non-empty one without TShockAPI.dll (a customer tidying the folder, or
 * a host copy gone stale against a newer image) boots with no TShock at all —
 * `Could not load file or assembly 'TShockAPI'` → "Startup aborted". A
 * separate folder + `-additionalplugins` leaves the image's own core volume
 * exactly as it is today.
 */
export const TERRARIA_PLUGIN_MOUNT = "/tshock/CustomPlugins";

 * WORLD_FILENAME it runs `./TShock.Server` bare, which drops to Terraria's
 * INTERACTIVE world-selection menu ("n  New World / d <number>  Delete
 * World") and waits forever on a stdin that never comes, so the game never
 * binds 7777. With WORLD_FILENAME set but no world file and no -autocreate
 * it exits 1 instead. Only both together generate a world and start.

 * recreating the container with these flags on a real VM, watching it
 * generate /opt/terraria/nxeon.wld and log "Server started", then connecting

 *    plugins hardcode "tshock/<file>" rather than asking TShock for its save

e4ba9938e7 Terraria: real one-click TShock plugin installs, verified on real servers
4512adb442 Fix real customer bug: Terraria GAME_POWER start falsely reported as failed

input.message:
## Summary

One-click Terraria mod install is built and tested on real hardware. It's on branch **`feature/terraria-real-mod-install`** (commit `e4ba9938e7`, pushed to origin). **Not merged and not promoted**: it changes a live product's provisioning script, so the owner needs to review the diff first.

**The bind-mount risk turned out to be real, so I didn't ship the scoped fix.** Mounting over `/tshock/ServerPlugins` can leave a server running without TShock at all. The shipped version uses a separate plugin folder instead (details below).

## What I verified on real containers

I provisioned two throwaway servers through the prod worker for this: `tmods-test-29d892` on node-2 and `tmods-test-0b3e24` on node-4, both owned by a new internal user `terraria-modtest@nxeon-internal.test`. No customer server was touched, including `throarbin-terraria`. **Both servers have since been deleted through normal DELETE jobs (both DONE).** The internal test user still exists, with no servers.

**Stock container before any change** (image `ryshe/terraria` sha256:b1c89f7f…, TShock 6.1.0.0, Terraria 1.4.5.6):
- `/tshock/ServerPlugins` is an anonymous Docker volume holding `TShockAPI.dll`, `.deps.json`, `.pdb` and `.xml`. TShock itself loads from there as a plugin: `[Server API] Info Plugin TShock v6.1.0.0 (by The TShock Team) initiated.`
- The image keeps an identical backup copy at `/plugins`. Its `bootstrap.sh` copies that back only when ServerPlugins is completely empty: `if [ -z "$(ls -A /tshock/ServerPlugins)" ]; then … cp /plugins/* /tshock/ServerPlugins`.

**Testing the scoped fix (mount over ServerPlugins):**
- **Empty host folder:** the defaults were not lost. The boot log showed `Copying plugins...`, the host folder got the same four files with matching sha256s, and TShock started.
- **Non-empty folder without `TShockAPI.dll`:** boot failed with `Could not load file or assembly 'TShockAPI, Version=5.2.0.0'` then `[Server API] Error Startup aborted…`. The world still loaded and logged `Server started`, so the server looks up while TShock is missing. A customer tidying that folder, or the host copy going stale against a newer image, would cause this.

**What I shipped instead:**
- A separate folder, `-v /opt/terraria-plugins:/tshock/CustomPlugins`, plus TShock's own `-additionalplugins /tshock/CustomPlugins` flag (confirmed present in this build's `TerrariaServer.dll`).
- A data alias, `-v /opt/terraria:/tshock/tshock`. Many plugins hardcode the `tshock/` folder, and Emojifier crashed startup without it (`Could not find a part of the path '/tshock/tshock/EmojifierConfig.json'`).
- I ran exactly what a Wipe & reinstall runs with the new script on both VMs. The container's Cmd ends in `"-additionalplugins","/tshock/CustomPlugins"`. ServerPlugins is still the untouched volume: same four files, same sha256s, image timestamps. TShock started with `Server started`.

**How an install works:** it downloads the author's latest GitHub release, which must be a single `.dll`, then restarts the server. It only marks the plugin INSTALLED if all of these hold, and otherwise removes it and restarts again:
- TShock logs a new "Plugin X initiated" line.
- Startup wasn't aborted.
- No crash is reported against that plugin.
- The server is still up 20 seconds later.

**The real worker code (the GAME_MOD_SYNC handler from the branch) against the node-4 server.** It ran against the prod DB for the test server only, with no Job row created, using hidden test catalogue rows that I deleted afterwards:
- **Stock container:** both mods failed with "This server was set up before one-click Terraria plugins were available…". Nothing was created on the VM and it wasn't restarted.
- **After switching to the new script:** `ComfyEconomy: status=INSTALLED version=1.5.7`.
- **Gravebags (known incompatible):** `status=FAILED error=Your server couldn't start with it installed (TShock: … Plugin "Gravebags" has thrown an exception during initialization.). It was removed again…`
- **Plugin effect without a game client:** ComfyEconomy's own `/bal`, run through TShock's local REST command endpoint, replied `"Only in-game players can check without giving a player name. Do this instead: /bal [player name]"`. A made-up command replied `"Invalid command entered."`
- **Removal:** the record was deleted, the file was gone, and the server restarted with only TShock loaded.

**Two bugs in my own first version, found on the real server and fixed:**
- BanGuard shuts the server down without an API key (`Error validating BanGuard API key`), and one of systemd's automatic restarts reached `Server started` before exiting again. The 20-second check now catches it: `BOOT:exited` then `ROLLBACK:ok`.
- The "was the server running?" check read systemd's pending-restart state as "stopped", which left the server stopped after every later install. Fixed and re-verified.

## Plugins seeded

The catalogue now has **23** TShock plugins:
- **Economy:** ComfyEconomy, PlaytimeRewards
- **Admin:** FACommands, Inventory Viewer, Region Extension, CustomItems, journeyUnlock, BossManager
- **Anti-cheat:** The Observer
- **Gameplay:** Bagger, TerraJump, IndividualLootChests, Boss Evolution, Tradekey
- **PvP / minigames:** Grace Period, No Teams, Pinger
- **Chat:** Emojifier, Show Armors
- **Quality of life:** BridgeBuilder, DisableRevenge
- **Compatibility:** SkipVersionCheck, MobileCrossplay

Checks on the list:
- All 23 were installed on a real server by the final install script. Each one came back installed, and the server was still running after each.
- All 23 resolve through the exact GitHub call the worker makes: latest release = the tested tag, exactly one `.dll`, download returns 200 at the expected size.
- Left out after testing, with reasons recorded in the script: PerPlayerLoot, QoL, PvPer, FloatingText-Chat, RankSystem, Gravebags, BanGuard, SteamEnablerPlugin, Skynomi-Extension, Abilities, and RegionsKLP (its author says it's for their own server only).
- Some plugins that loaded fine were left out editorially because their in-game text is Chinese-only.

The seed script also replaces the Terraria template's setup script and retires the 1000 tModLoader Steam Workshop rows (deleted, since nothing references them). **I applied it to `nxeon_staging` for real, and a second run changed nothing. Production data is untouched** (still 1000 steam_workshop rows).

Other changes on the branch:
- Terraria only shows Install buttons for GitHub plugins, whether or not the reseed has run.
- The importers no longer re-add tModLoader content.
- The public mods-page copy no longer says Terraria uses tModLoader.

Checks: `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and the new plus related tests pass (66/66). One unrelated test, `portal-ui-audit`, also fails on current main. `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` has a dated entry and `ROADMAP.md` is updated. I didn't run `publish-docs.mjs` because this is an unmerged branch.

## For the owner
- **Rollout:** `NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon npx tsx scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts` (dry run), then add `--apply`, then promote. Either order is safe.
- **Existing servers:** the 2 live Terraria servers (`terraria-i2ydef`, `throarbin-terraria`) are not migrated. They'll get the honest "contact support" message. Enabling one means recreating its container with the new flags; the world and TShock data in `/opt/terraria` are kept. That's a per-server decision for the owner.
- **node-2 networking issue:** node-2 sometimes answered the test VM's SSH port (`178.63.94.114:20038`) from a different machine with a different host key, and the VM had intermittent DNS failures. That looks like a duplicate internal IP, which could affect a real customer. I flagged it as a follow-up task. I didn't dig further because the permission system blocked reading node-2 directly.
- **Probable backup bug (not verified on a real backup):** Terraria world backups probably fail. The world sits directly in `/opt/terraria` on the host, but none of the folders the backup and Worlds-tab code checks for Terraria exist there. Worth a follow-up; I couldn't flag it myself because the task tool timed out.
- **Marketing copy:** the Terraria marketing pages still advertise tModLoader, Calamity and Thorium, which Nxeon doesn't run.
- **Known gap:** Wipe & reinstall clears plugin folders but leaves install records saying INSTALLED. Every file-drop game has the same problem; it isn't new here.

Worktree is `/root/nxeon-worktrees/terraria-mods`. Main files: `lib/terraria-plugins.ts`, `worker/game-mods.ts`, `lib/mod-install-support.ts`, `prisma/catalog.ts`, `scripts/seed-terraria-tshock-plugins.ts`, `test/terraria-plugins.test.ts`.

- **Stock container:** both mods failed with "This server was set up before one-click Terraria plugins were available…". Nothing was created on the VM and it wasn't restarted.
- **After switching to the new script:** `ComfyEconomy: status=INSTALLED version=1.5.7`.

**Two bugs in my own first version, found on the real server and fixed:**
- BanGuard shuts the server down without an API key (`Error validating BanGuard API key`), and one of systemd's automatic restarts reached `Server started` before exiting again. The 20-second check now catches it: `BOOT:exited` then `ROLLBACK:ok`.
- The "was the server running?" check read systemd's pending-restart state as "stopped", which left the server stopped after every later install. Fixed and re-verified.
